THE ORDER is frequency, the commonest word first — for a reader that is the order that reaches a page soonest — with one rule added: a small closed set arrives together, where its commonest member falls. So the first cards are {fact.firstFive}; wesan and bēon, one verb in two stems, follow as notes {fact.beAt} and {fact.beTo}; iċ, þū, wē and ġē come on day {fact.weDay}; willan, magan, sċulan, mōtan, cunnan and witan on day {fact.modalDay}; mīn, þīn, ūre and ēower on day {fact.possDay}; the {fact.askN} question words on day {fact.askDay}; the numbers above one on day {fact.numDay}. No card was added and none removed: a level is a band of frequency, and six, eight, nine and ten are Level 2's by count. THE PACE: the default is ten new cards a day, both directions together, which is five words a day; with the alphabet deck first, this deck runs from day {from} to day {to}.
